chapter: Luck, tricks and the Bourbon Street job
title: The tight-fisted Italian owner and the boxcar-liquor grocer
summary: The stingy Italian owner whom Kid could always get things from, then a lucky grocer who bought liquor by the boxcar and the story of his killing an oil man.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

Look, that man wouldn't know how he want to give you a drink of water. You hear me? I used to wait for him. See, you see like a drink? Man, he would never give you nothing to drink. But look, I was the only fella who could get something out of him. And everybody would work for him. He said, kid, you the only man can do something with that man. You know how I get him, Mr. Bill? You see like some fella come there, some white fella may come there and talk with him. You know what you do? He like, he give you that ballroom. If he got company. And you go there and ask him. He like, take the whole ballroom. See? But after that, otherwise, he didn't give you nothing. But I always could get something out of him. You see, I'd get out of him all right, no? So, well, his girlfriend bought him out. And that man really had, people used to come there. The place couldn't hold the people. That's right. So he was wondering how the fella did it. I told him, I said, listen. I said, I'm going to tell you how the fella did it. I said, you the fella like to, you like to all for all. I said, but this man didn't even give him. I said, you got to give some time too. I said, then you're gaining in front of the people. You see what I mean? But he was a tight fella, man. He wouldn't give nothing, not him. See? So, and he's a fella, he tried everything. You know him, Billy? He never could hardly make it. So somebody told me that he left and he went on away from here. Some of the country, some parts of the country, where I left. So, well, them fella, that fella, that fella in Speck was the luckiest man over there. Now that fella used to buy liquor by the boxcar. Really?
You know what the man said? The salesman said? That man used to buy more liquor in this, and any of this bar in this city.
Got a good price on it then too, that way. That's right.

And you know what he used to do, Mr. Bill? He'd come and buy his liquor. All he needed for his grocery itself. He didn't allow no drummer. You know why? He had a drummer. He went and got the sheriff, well all the, everybody over there noticed man, the color fella. So, you see when they come there? They was afraid of him. Cause he in the house now, you see, Mr. Bill had the trouble, the fire gonna come to get you, you ain't here. He don't know what you had. Well, the man, the man, the man, the man, they want him to pay for something he didn't got. That's how he come to, you know, you see what I mean? So, well, all right. So what this man did, well, what he done, he fooled around, that's why he didn't allow no drummers. See, from, after that he didn't allow no drummers, he used to come, he had one of them great big old Cadillacs. He load up, see? Everything he wanted, he had stuff all on top of the car, in the car and everything, so he couldn't hardly see me in the car, you know what I mean? So he keep the trouble down, he come in over here, he used to go right on, party street, wholesale, get all the stuff there. It's on set, you know? Go to liquor places, and get all the liquor you want, you see? Box car, he used to buy his liquor. So, so they have to keep the drummers from there, cause he had trouble with that fella. So well now, him and Speck, his luckiest two people was over that river, for business. And Speck is a man made more money than anybody been running dance over that river. That's right. Yeah.
